Byomkesh.description: The protagonist and sharp detective known as a 'truth-seeker' or 'satyanweshi' who solves mysteries using keen observation and logic.

Ajit.description: The narrator and close friend of Byomkesh, who documents their adventures and assists in investigations.

Ramanath Neogi.description: A notorious jewel thief, recently released from jail, whose past crime and actions are central to the mystery.

Maharaja Ramendra Sinha.description: A wealthy and benevolent aristocrat, owner of the stolen blue diamond, who seeks Byomkesh's help after his secretary's murder.

Haripada Rakshit.description: The Maharaja's secretary, a reformed criminal with a history of imprisonment, whose murder is the focus of the investigation.

Nirmal babu.description: A retired and intelligent police detective who previously investigated the theft of the blue diamond.

Bidhu babu.description: A police inspector involved in the current investigation, sometimes referred to by the variant name Buddhu babu.

Purna babu.description: The police officer in charge of the murder investigation of Haripada Rakshit.

Putiram.description: A servant or helper in Byomkesh's household, who assists with household tasks.

Raktamukhi Neela.description: The Bengali title of the story, translating to 'The Deadly Diamond', referring to the central object of the mystery.

Saratchandra.description: Refers to Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay, a famous Bengali novelist, whose work 'Charitraheen' is mentioned.

Charitraheen.description: A well-known novel by Saratchandra Chattopadhyay, referenced here as being shown in cinema halls.

Alipur.description: A locality in Calcutta (now Kolkata), known for its jail, which plays a role in the story.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in India where the events of the story take place.

Jawaharlal Hiralal.description: A jeweller or jewellery shop in Calcutta, mentioned as a victim of theft.

Dutta jewellers.description: Another jewellery shop in Calcutta, also burgled during the spate of thefts.

Marwari.description: An Indian ethnic group, often associated with business and trade, referenced here in the context of buying diamonds.

Saturn.description: The planet, referenced in Indian astrology as being associated with blue diamonds and their supposed powers.

Rolls Royce.description: A luxury British car, symbolizing the wealth and status of Maharaja Ramendra Sinha.

babu.description: A respectful term used in Bengal and other parts of India to address men, often appended to names or titles.

lakhs.description: A unit in the Indian numbering system equal to one hundred thousand (100,000).

jailbird.description: A colloquial term for someone who has spent a significant amount of time in jail, often used in Indian English.

matinee.description: A term used in India for an afternoon cinema show or performance, here used metaphorically for a dramatic event.
